```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Global options: hide code, suppress warnings, centre all figures
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo      = FALSE,
  warning   = FALSE,
  message   = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center"
)

# Packages
# tidyverse - data wrangling and ggplot2 charts
# scales    - formats numbers with commas and % on axes
# knitr + kableExtra - for PDF-friendly tables (same as KCSE / Embu reports)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```

```{r load-results-data, include=FALSE}
# Results are built here (hidden) so summary statistics are available for the
# Executive Summary below. The same code is shown, for transparency, in the
# "Data Entry" section under Data and Methodology further down.
candidates <- data.frame(
  Candidate = c("Abdifatah Hussein Abdullahi", "Timothy Kamau Kasuku",
                "Wilson Mwaniki Kigwa", "Edwin Kariri Muchiri",
                "Edward Mathenge Mwaniki", "Rachael Wangui Njoroge",
                "Samuel Muchina Nyagah", "Stephen Wanyoike Waithaka",
                "Sammy Douglas Kamau Waweru"),
  Party     = c("PPS", "PM", "Jubilee", "PNU", "KMA", "PDP",
                "UDA", "NLP", "DCP"),
  Votes     = c(19, 51, 198, 28, 16, 11, 5450, 103, 35440)
)

candidates$Share_Pct <- round(candidates$Votes / sum(candidates$Votes) * 100, 1)
candidates <- candidates[order(-candidates$Votes), ]

registered_voters <- 73480
total_turnout     <- 41656
valid_votes        <- sum(candidates$Votes)
rejected_ballots  <- 340

turnout_pct  <- round(total_turnout / registered_voters * 100, 1)
rejected_pct <- round(rejected_ballots / total_turnout * 100, 1)

winner    <- candidates[1, ]
runner_up <- candidates[2, ]

margin_votes <- winner$Votes - runner_up$Votes
margin_pct   <- round(margin_votes / valid_votes * 100, 1)
```

\newpage

# Executive Summary

This report analyses the results of the Ol Kalou Constituency by-election for
Member of National Assembly, as declared on **Form 35B** by the IEBC
Constituency Returning Officer. Nine candidates contested the seat.

**Key figures at a glance:** **`r winner$Candidate`** (`r winner$Party`) won
the seat with **`r comma(winner$Votes)`** votes (**`r winner$Share_Pct`%** of
valid votes cast), ahead of **`r runner_up$Candidate`** (`r runner_up$Party`)
on `r comma(runner_up$Votes)` votes — a margin of **`r comma(margin_votes)`
votes (`r margin_pct` percentage points)**. Of `r comma(registered_voters)`
registered voters, `r comma(total_turnout)` turned out to vote
(**`r turnout_pct`%** turnout), of which `r comma(rejected_ballots)` ballots
(`r rejected_pct`%) were rejected.

\newpage

# Data and Methodology

## Data Entry

Figures below are the constituency-level aggregate results as declared on
Form 35B. The code is shown here for transparency; it was already run
earlier (see the hidden `load-results-data` chunk) so that summary statistics
could feed into the Executive Summary above.

```{r data-listing, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
candidates <- data.frame(
  Candidate = c("Abdifatah Hussein Abdullahi", "Timothy Kamau Kasuku",
                "Wilson Mwaniki Kigwa", "Edwin Kariri Muchiri",
                "Edward Mathenge Mwaniki", "Rachael Wangui Njoroge",
                "Samuel Muchina Nyagah", "Stephen Wanyoike Waithaka",
                "Sammy Douglas Kamau Waweru"),
  Party     = c("PPS", "PM", "Jubilee", "PNU", "KMA", "PDP",
                "UDA", "NLP", "DCP"),
  Votes     = c(19, 51, 198, 28, 16, 11, 5450, 103, 35440)
)

# Vote share per candidate, sorted from largest to smallest
candidates$Share_Pct <- round(candidates$Votes / sum(candidates$Votes) * 100, 1)
candidates <- candidates[order(-candidates$Votes), ]

# Turnout figures, as declared on the form
registered_voters <- 73480
total_turnout     <- 41656
valid_votes       <- sum(candidates$Votes)  # cross-checked against the form
rejected_ballots  <- 340
```

## Methodology

Results were compiled from the Form 35B declaration for Ol Kalou Constituency
(Code 091). Analysis was conducted in R to compute:

- Candidate vote share (% of valid votes)
- Margin of victory between the top two candidates
- Voter turnout (% of registered voters)
- Rejected ballots (% of total votes cast)

### Limitations

- This report uses **constituency-level aggregate results only** (the
  candidate totals and voter turnout figures printed on Form 35B). The
  scanned copy of the form carries a security watermark that makes the
  underlying **polling-station-level** breakdown (140+ stations) unreliable
  to extract by OCR; those figures were not used here to avoid introducing
  transcription errors.
- All aggregate figures were cross-checked for internal consistency
  (candidate votes sum to the stated valid votes total; valid votes plus
  rejected ballots equal the stated turnout figure) before use.
- The report covers a single constituency by-election and does not draw
  conclusions about wider county- or national-level trends.

\newpage

# Results Analysis

## Candidate Vote Share

```{r candidate-table}
candidates[, c("Candidate", "Party", "Votes", "Share_Pct")] |>
  kable(
    booktabs    = TRUE,
    caption     = "Ol Kalou By-Election Results by Candidate",
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    col.names   = c("Candidate", "Party", "Votes", "Share (%)"),
    align       = "llrr",
    row.names   = FALSE
  ) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) |>
  row_spec(1, background = "#eafaf1")
```

```{r candidate-bar, fig.cap="Candidate Vote Share — Ol Kalou By-Election", fig.height=4.5}
# Horizontal bar chart, ordered by votes, with % share labelled at bar end
ggplot(candidates, aes(x = reorder(Candidate, Votes), y = Votes, fill = Party)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Share_Pct, "%")), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title   = "Candidate Vote Share — Ol Kalou By-Election",
    x       = "",
    y       = "Votes",
    caption = "Source: IEBC Form 35B, Ol Kalou Constituency (Code 091)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

### Observation

The contest was effectively a two-way race: `r winner$Candidate`
(`r winner$Party`) and `r runner_up$Candidate` (`r runner_up$Party`) together
took **`r round(winner$Share_Pct + runner_up$Share_Pct, 1)`%** of all valid
votes, while the remaining seven candidates shared just
**`r round(100 - winner$Share_Pct - runner_up$Share_Pct, 1)`%** between them.

## Margin of Victory

```{r margin-table}
margin_table <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Winner", "Runner-up", "Margin (votes)", "Margin (% of valid votes)"),
  Value  = c(
    paste0(winner$Candidate, " (", winner$Party, ") — ", comma(winner$Votes)),
    paste0(runner_up$Candidate, " (", runner_up$Party, ") — ", comma(runner_up$Votes)),
    comma(margin_votes),
    paste0(margin_pct, "%")
  )
)

kable(
  margin_table,
  booktabs  = TRUE,
  caption   = "Margin of Victory",
  col.names = c("Metric", "Value"),
  align     = "ll"
) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

## Voter Turnout and Rejected Ballots

```{r turnout-table}
turnout_table <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Registered Voters", "Total Turnout", "Valid Votes",
             "Rejected Ballots", "Turnout (%)", "Rejected Ballots (% of turnout)"),
  Value  = c(
    comma(registered_voters),
    comma(total_turnout),
    comma(valid_votes),
    comma(rejected_ballots),
    paste0(turnout_pct, "%"),
    paste0(rejected_pct, "%")
  )
)

kable(
  turnout_table,
  booktabs  = TRUE,
  caption   = "Voter Turnout Summary",
  col.names = c("Metric", "Value"),
  align     = "lr"
) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

```{r turnout-chart, fig.cap="Votes Cast: Valid vs. Rejected", fig.height=2.5}
# Single stacked bar showing valid vs. rejected as parts of total votes cast
cast_long <- data.frame(
  Category = "Votes Cast",
  Type     = c("Valid", "Rejected"),
  Count    = c(valid_votes, rejected_ballots)
)
cast_long$Type <- factor(cast_long$Type, levels = c("Rejected", "Valid"))

ggplot(cast_long, aes(x = Category, y = Count, fill = Type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Valid" = "#27ae60", "Rejected" = "#c0392b"), name = "") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Votes", caption = "Source: IEBC Form 35B, Ol Kalou Constituency (Code 091)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    axis.text.y      = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

### Observation

Turnout stood at `r turnout_pct`% of registered voters — typical for a
by-election, where turnout is usually lower than in general elections.
Rejected ballots were a small share of votes cast (`r rejected_pct`%),
suggesting no major spoilage issue at the constituency level.

\newpage

# Conclusions and Recommendations

## Conclusions

1. **Decisive Win** — `r winner$Candidate` (`r winner$Party`) won the seat
   with `r winner$Share_Pct`% of valid votes, a margin of
   `r comma(margin_votes)` votes over the runner-up.

2. **Two-Party Dominance** — The top two candidates captured
   `r round(winner$Share_Pct + runner_up$Share_Pct, 1)`% of valid votes
   between them, leaving little room for the other seven candidates.

3. **Moderate Turnout** — At `r turnout_pct`%, turnout was moderate,
   consistent with typical by-election patterns where general disengagement
   or a widely-anticipated result can depress participation.

4. **Low Ballot Rejection** — Rejected ballots made up only `r rejected_pct`%
   of votes cast, indicating voters largely understood how to cast a valid
   vote.

## Recommendations

- **Verify polling-station-level data separately** — If station-level
  analysis (e.g. identifying low-turnout polling stations for future voter
  education) is required for this assignment, obtain a clean-text source
  (e.g. the IEBC results portal or a verified transcription) rather than
  relying on OCR of the watermarked scan.

- **Investigate turnout drivers** — Future work could compare this
  by-election's turnout against the constituency's turnout in the last
  general election to assess whether the drop (if any) is typical for
  by-elections.

- **Monitor competitiveness trends** — With such a wide margin, future
  reports could track whether the dominant party's vote share is stable or
  shrinking across successive elections in this constituency.
